newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek Cypriots remember, condemn 1974 coup.
newsitem.headline: Greek Cypriots remember, condemn 1974 coup.

text.p: Air raid sirens wailed over divided Cyprus on Tuesday in remembrance of a Greek-backed coup 23 years ago which led to Turkey's invasion of northern Cyprus five days later.

The sirens blared across most towns of the eastern Mediterranean island for a minute at 8.20 a.m. (05.20 GMT), marking the hour when rebel forces launched their attack, led by officers of the Greek junta then ruling Athens.
The late president, Archbishop Makarios, escaped from the presidential palace in the capital Nicosia while it was under attack by rebel troops. He was flown out of Cyprus by British forces.

The coup sparked the intervention of Turkey, one of the guarantor powers of Cyprus under the 1960 treaty that gave the former British colony independence. It invaded Cyprus on July 20, 1974, saying it wanted to protect the island's Turkish Cypriot community.
During the invasion the coup collapsed, as did the Athens junta, but Cyprus remains divided.
Memorial services were held in memory of the victims and a special session of parliament was scheduled to condemn the coup.

Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides, as Greek Cypriot leader, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are currently engaged in negotiations under United Nations auspices to reunite the Mediterranean island as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.
